test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 04 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A train overtakes two persons walking along a railway track. The first one walks at 5.4 km/hr. The other one walks at 18 km/hr. The train needs 30 and 44 seconds, respectively, to overtake them. What is the speed of the train, if both the persons are walking in the same direction as the train?
solution:
**Given:**

Speed of first person = 5.4 km/hr

Speed of second person = 18 km/hr

Time = 30 sec and 44 sec

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed = (Train speed - Person speed)

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let speed of train = x m/s

⇒ 5.4 km/hr = 1.5 m/s

⇒ 18 km/hr = 5 m/s

⇒ Train length = (x - 1.5) × 30

⇒ Train length = (x - 5) × 44

⇒ (x - 1.5) × 30 = (x - 5) × 44

⇒ 30x - 45 = 44x - 220

⇒ 220 - 45 = 44x - 30x

⇒ 175 = 14x

⇒ x = 12.5 m/s

⇒ Speed in km/hr = 12.5 × 18/5

⇒ Speed = 45

**∴ The correct answer is 45 km/hr.**
